title: Image overlap odp 001
notes: honest category divergence (same call as the pptx counterpart): presentation formats have NO text-wrap concept — wrap is a wordprocessing feature — so this is a z-order overlap test, not a text-wrap test. A deterministic opaque solid-ink 64x48 PNG (PIL, no rng) sits at Pictures/wrap1.png (manifest media-type image/png) in draw:frame > draw:image, placed by automatic graphic style gpPic (fo:x/fo:y 1in, 4in x 2.2in, draw:z-index=0); the presentation:body frame (named graphic style gp1: fo:x 0.5in, fo:y 1.9in, 9in x 5in, draw:z-index=1) covers x 0.5..9.5in y 1.9..6.9in and therefore overlaps the picture's lower-right corner region 1..5 x 1.9..3.2in. Later document order + higher draw:z-index both say the text frame paints on top (asserted: WrapPic1 precedes Body1). Honest caveats: gp1 is fill-less so whether the frame is transparent over the raster is renderer policy, and LibreOffice was not run here. The picture carries no text; reference text is the three frame lines. Normative counters read draw:frame=2.
